title: Human Approval Is Part Of The Execution Model

slides.author: Alexey Grigorev
slides.title: Human approval is not just a button
slides.subtitle: When an agent waits for a person, the workflow needs durable state.

slides.title: The diagram looks simple
slides.body: The agent prepares an action. A person reviews it. The agent continues. That looks small in code.

slides.title: Waiting changes the system
slides.body: Approval can take two hours or two days. The worker can restart. A deploy can finish while the workflow is paused.

slides.title: Approval needs storage
slides.body: The workflow should write pending approval state, keep the workflow ID, and store the proposed action.

slides.title: Resume from the event
slides.body: When the approval event arrives, the workflow should continue from that step. It should not depend on one Python process still being alive.

slides.title: Workshop focus
slides.body: Nicholas Lotz will cover human-in-the-loop workflows, retries, timeouts, traces, recovery, and deployment patterns.

slides.supportingText: Running Durable Agents in Production, June 16, 4:30-6:00 PM GMT+2 on YouTube.
